mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the role/op permission constraint and forcing a Doctor to succeed at the admin-only ListAudit endpoint produces an instance where a Permitted operation falls outside PermMatrix.Allowed — exactly what LeastPrivilege rules out.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Permitted and op.caller.userRole = Doctor and op.opKind = ListAudit }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the audit-completeness fact and inserting an authenticated RecordLookup that has no audit entry breaks the one-audit-per-clinical-access invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some op: Operation | some op.authenticated and op.opKind = RecordLookup and (no ae: AuditEntry | ae.ofOperation = op) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Without care-team gating, a Permitted RecordLookup can exist for a caller with no membership row — directly violating the ownership-based access invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamGatingViolation { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Permitted and op.opKind = RecordLookup and (no ct: CareTeamMembership | ct.ctClinician = op.caller and ct.ctPatient = op.targetPatient and some ct.ctActive) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Without the snapshot-equality fact, an AuditEntry can record a different user than the operation's actual caller — a textbook misattribution counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.auditUser != ae.ofOperation.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the response-shape fact and forcing two non-Permitted operations to differ in externalResponse reveals the existence/non-existence distinction that FR-006 forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeakageViolation { some disj op1, op2: Operation | op1.outcome = Denied and op2.outcome = NotFoundOrDenied and op1.externalResponse != op2.externalResponse }

mutation_targets.rationale: Without the unique-creator constraint, two distinct operations can share a ClinicalNote — the cleanest static stand-in for note mutation/duplication that append-only rules out.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj op1, op2: Operation | some op1.createdNote and op1.createdNote = op2.createdNote }
